subject: Initial MSA intake — party identity verification + redline triage
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@acmeapp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MSA intake — quick checklist and who does what

Hi Emma —

Thanks for sending over the MSA draft earlier. I pulled the doc and attached a short party sheet to confirm identities and signing authorities before our legal team does a formal redline. Goal: avoid churn on basic party/billing/residency facts so redlines focus on substance.

Quick asks from our side to unblock contracting:
- Confirm legal entity name to appear in the MSA (exact, with punctuation).
- Billing legal entity and invoice email (if different from signer).
- Primary signer name, title, and authority cutoff (who can sign without board approval).
- Operational region(s) for data residency (US/EU/APAC) and whether they require specific residency carveouts.

If you can share the final PO number (if already generated) and the procurement contact at payments+procurement@acmeapp.com that helps timeline estimates.

We’ll do an initial pass from our side and return a prioritized set of redlines: Blockers (SLA/residency/data flow), Negotiable (payment/billing), and Boilerplate (definitions/typos).

Attached: party sheet stub — please fill or confirm. We’ll schedule a 30-min sync if it’s easier.

Thanks —
Sergio
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Party_Sheet_Acme.csv (text/csv)]

Subject: Re: Initial MSA intake — quick checklist and who does what

Hi Sergio —

Thanks — confirming below inline and attached an org-signed entity proof.

- Legal entity: AcmeApp, Inc. (exact)
- Billing entity: AcmeApp, Inc. — invoices to billing@acmeapp.com
- Primary signer: Emma Li, VP Finance — delegated authority up to $500k. For amounts >$500k we need CFO sign-off (Tom Nguyen).
- Data residency: US default; for certain regulated customers we’ll discuss EU regional options (not required here).

PO is being routed — expected PO# in ~3 business days. Procurement contact is payments+procurement@acmeapp.com (copying Tom).

I attached a signed certificate page and the Acme internal signer matrix. Please let me know if you need a copy with a wet signature.

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA intake — quick checklist and who does what

Thanks Emma / Sergio — copying initial legal triage.

I pulled the draft and did a 1st-pass markup focused on items likely to impact go-live timing. I’m attaching a tracked version (Acme_MSA_Draft_v1_redlines.docx) and a short decision table below.

Priority buckets (recommendation):
1) Blockers — need commercial sign-off prior to any counterparty negotiation:
   - Section 6 (Data residency): clarify where Redwood will process keys/hosted inference; flag for possible Exhibit on residency.
   - Section 9 (Security & Audit): Acme requested SOC2 Type II evidence and a 30-day access window for audits — propose standard audit window language plus security questionnaire response instead of ad-hoc audit right.
2) Commercial negotiables — can land in order form or exhibit:
   - Termination for convenience notice and cure periods.
   - Payment net terms: default 30 vs Acme’s ask of 45 — flag for finance.
3) Boilerplate / low risk: indemnities, definitions cleanup, clause numbering.

Action items for internal owners:
- Sergio: confirm whether we will commit to the 30-day audit window or propose an alternate (Jonas suggests security questionnaire + annual review).
- Marissa: confirm billing/contact and whether we accept Net 45 or push to Net 30.
- Jonas (security): prepare proposed alternate language for audit & data residency by EOD tomorrow.

Emma / Tom — if any of the above mischaracterizes Acme’s asks, flag and we’ll revise. If you prefer, we can schedule an internal triage meeting (15–20m) with procurement + security to accelerate.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Acme_MSA_Draft_v1_redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA intake — quick checklist and who does what

Quick follow-up from security perspective —

I agree with the triage. Proposed compromise for the audit/data residency asks:
- Add Exhibit X outlining data residency commitments scoped to the order form(s) where required; do not bake EU residency into the base MSA.
- For audit rights: we accept a documented security questionnaire + one scheduled annual onsite/remote audit with 30 days’ notice; deny open-ended immediate audit requests.

I’ll draft suggested language and include fallback phrasing that permits a time-boxed on-site review with a mutually agreeable scope. Sending draft in a separate email in ~2 hours.

If procurement insists on shorter payment terms we should escalate pricing or include a short-term credit hold path; Marissa — can you advise on commercial sensitivity if we propose Net 30?

Jonas
Director, InfoSec — Redwood Inference

On scheduling: I’m available Mon 11:00–12:30 or Tue 09:00–11:00 PST for a quick alignment call if needed.
